record.title: CS/CS/CS/HB 369 (2025): Provenance of Digital Content
record.short_title: Florida HB 369 (2025): provenance of AI-generated content
record.issuing_body: Florida House of Representatives (2025 Regular Session; Commerce Committee and Rep. McFarland)
record.summary: Bill that would have required developers of publicly available generative AI tools to offer a tool letting users apply provenance data to synthetic content made with the developer's tool, or to apply such data themselves where technically feasible, and to make a free provenance reader available. Provenance data, following widely adopted standards, would show whether visual content is synthetic and name the developer, without personally identifying information. Social media platforms would have had to retain available provenance data and make it accessible to users. Violations would have been unfair or deceptive practices, enforced only by the Attorney General after a 30-day cure period.
record.notes: Filed 4 Feb 2025. Reported favourably with committee substitutes by the Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee (17-0, 19 Mar 2025), the Economic Infrastructure Subcommittee (16-0, 31 Mar 2025) and the Commerce Committee (25-0, 15 Apr 2025). The first substitute dropped provisions of the filed version on disclaimers on election materials, a pilot programme at the Division of Emergency Management and capture devices; the Commerce Committee replaced 'provider' with 'developer', removed audio from 'synthetic content' and excluded services that exclusively provide video game experiences. The bill would have created s. 501.9741, F.S., with an effective date of 1 Jul 2026. Placed on the House Second Reading Calendar, temporarily postponed on 23 Apr 2025, indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration on 3 May 2025, and died on the Second Reading Calendar on 16 Jun 2025. The similar Senate bill SB 702 (Burgess) died in the Ethics and Elections Committee.

verification.note: Stored the Florida Senate bill page for HB 369 (2025), with its history, versions, amendments and related bills; the text of the third committee substitute (CS/CS/CS/HB 369, filed 16 Apr 2025), the last version of the bill; and the House staff analyses of the Information Technology Budget & Policy Subcommittee (20 Mar 2025), the Economic Infrastructure Subcommittee (1 Apr 2025) and the Commerce Committee (17 Apr 2025) (all flsenate.gov). The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, filing date, committee actions and the 'Died on Second Reading Calendar' action of 16 Jun 2025; the summary follows the text of the third committee substitute.

judgment.status_reasoning: Latest event: 'Died on Second Reading Calendar' in the House on 16 Jun 2025, after the bill was temporarily postponed on second reading (23 Apr 2025) and indefinitely postponed and withdrawn from consideration (3 May 2025). It never passed either chamber and has no chapter law; the 2025 session is over, so as of 14 Oct 2026 it has no effect. A bill that died stays 'Proposed' with status 'Lapsed' (AGENTS.md section 5.6; precedent US-FL-01). date_published is the filing date; date_last_updated is the filing of the third committee substitute, the last version of the text.
judgment.scope_reasoning: In scope with no scope_note: an AI-specific bill on provenance labelling of content generated or modified by generative AI, with duties on AI providers and social media platforms. Lapsed bills are kept for context (AGENTS.md section 10).
judgment.summary_reasoning: The summary follows the text of the third committee substitute (hb369-03-c3), the last version of the bill, checked against the Commerce Committee analysis of 17 Apr 2025. Defined terms are rendered as the bill gives them: 'generative artificial intelligence developer' (the Commerce Committee replaced 'provider'), 'provenance data', 'provenance application tool', 'provenance reader', and 'synthetic content', which in this version covers visual content only.
